business_problem: Unilever needed a faster way to explore huge materials and chemistry search spaces for product R&D without relying solely on slow, resource-intensive physical experiments.
solution_summary: Unilever is using Azure Quantum Elements as the computational core of its DataLab environment to accelerate materials discovery in research and development. Researchers query scientific information through Microsoft Copilot for Azure, then use Azure high-performance computing and Azure Quantum Elements to run thousands of simulations far faster than physical lab work alone could support. The outputs from those simulations are fed back into models that screen tens of thousands of candidate materials and explore chemical reactions before laboratory teams commit to experiments. By making simulation and natural-language exploration part of the discovery funnel, Unilever turns its proprietary science data and R&D expertise into a scalable digital workflow. The platform helps scientists search broader molecular spaces, refine formulations for brands such as Dove and TRESemmé, and move sustainability and product-innovation work forward with materially faster iteration.

evidence_quotes: Unilever is bringing its digital vision to life through the transformational DataLab—its digital counterpart to the company’s physical laboratories—with the help of Microsoft Azure.

With Copilot in Azure, Azure high-performance computing, and the advanced simulation capabilities of Azure Quantum Elements, Unilever can query scientific information using natural language, performing thousands of computational simulations in the time it would take to run tens of laboratory experiments.
Unilever scientists can use the data gathered from these simulations to fine-tune models that screen tens of thousands of materials.
